key_insight: Transporting phase-averaged concentration keeps scalars confined to the front-tracked phase while preserving total mass.
engineering_relevance: The method improves scalar fidelity in multiphase-flow simulations where leakage across interfaces can distort concentrations and surfactant effects.
method: Divide cell-averaged concentration by phase fraction, then linearly extend it across the interface and advect.
Rebuild cell-averaged concentration using the tracked front’s volume-preserving phase fraction.
Apply a uniform phase-averaged concentration shift to restore total mass.
evidence_signal: Across five 3D tests, the method reduced error by more than tenfold at the finest resolution in four non-surfactant cases and kept surfactant inside the bubble where direct transport leaked 5.5–24% into the wake.
watch_item: Implementation must carefully handle division by small phase fractions and assess how the uniform mass correction affects local concentrations.
paper_title: Mass-conservative and phase-consistent transport of phase-confined scalars in front tracking
